text:
alex: quick heads-up — seeing a weird all-reduce tail after enabling LL128 channels on 8xA100. latency tail up ~30-40%. traces suggest kernel selector flips to a generic kernel mid-step and then we start preempting other collectives. attaching notes.

chris: you mean NCCL_PROTO=LL128 + NCCL_ALGO=RING?

alex: yes. proto=LL128, algo=ring (default). warmups look fine for ~200 iters, then one rank stalls in prep and others fall back. nvprof shows kernels recompiled/selected at runtime. snippet below: 
```
Time(ms)   Kernel                           Grid   Block
0.56       allreduce_ll128_ring             1024   256
2.92       allreduce_generic                2048   128  <-- regression
```

jin: can you paste the NCCL env you used?

alex: NCCL_ALGO=RING
NCCL_PROTO=LL128
NCCL_MAX_RINGS=8
NCCL_COLLNET=0
RUNTIME_KERN_SEL=1

maria: saw something similar on small sequence lengths when KV cache hit patterns are bursty. our kernel selector picks a fast kernel for the common shape, but fragmented batches cause it to fall back, creating compute imbalance -> allreduce queueing.

chris: do you have microbench numbers?

alex: baseline tokens/s ~2200 -> 1600 after the regression. allreduce 1-step latency 0.6ms -> 3.2ms on the slow steps. nvlink utilization graph shows link idle spikes coincident with fallback.

ops-bot: deploy manifest update pushed to ci/runtime/ll128-fallback-sweep (build 4721).

maria: quick proposal: demote LL128 to LL when fragmentation > threshold, or switch to algo=tree for <X byte messages. also tune NCCL_LL_THRESHOLD (lower it) so we avoid LL128 choosing for small fragmented payloads.

chris: I'll schedule a parameter sweep: NCCL_LL_THRESHOLD=256,512,1024 + NCCL_MAX_RINGS=4/8 + NCCL_ALGO=RING/TREE. 8 jobs, overnight.

jin: add kernel selector verbose logging and per-op trace. also run with kv-cache stress (patterned prefix hits) to reproduce.

alex: attaching a perf heatmap (per-step allreduce times) as soon as CI job finishes.

ci-bot: benchmark job queued #4587 :hourglass_flowing_sand:

maria: if sweep confirms, we should add an auto-fallback heuristic in runtime: if allreduce latency > 2ms for 3 consecutive windows -> switch proto/algo for that shard for N steps and emit a rollout flag. evict the kernel cache entry that caused the fallback.

chris: agreed. I'll prototype policy in runtime (short-circuit decision based on per-channel smoothed latency). if it works we can expose as config on Dedicated and Private.

alex: thanks. tagging @maria @chris — will post traces + nvprof tarball here when CI done.
